Writing bare metal assembly code involves directly interacting with the hardware without an operating system. Here's a simple example for x86 architecture that sets up a basic environment and enters an infinite loop:

```asm
[BITS 16]            ; 16-bit real mode
[ORG 0x7C00]         ; Bootloader starts at 0x7C00

; Set up the stack
mov ax, 0x0000
mov ss, ax
mov sp, 0xFFFF

; Clear the screen
mov ah, 0x00
mov al, 0x03
int 0x10

; Enter an infinite loop
jmp $

; Padding and magic number
times 510-($-$$) db 0
dw 0xAA55
```

This code sets up a basic stack, clears the screen, and then enters an infinite loop. It's a simple example of what a bootloader might do.
